info.title: Catch Public API
info.description:
The complete inventory of publicly reachable machine endpoints currently implemented by Catch. Pairing creates one device token. That token is used to submit captures for the account that owns the device.

**Try it out sends real requests to the current Catch installation.** Pairing consumes a valid setup code, and capture requests store data.

Routes marked **Reserved** exist in the application, but pairing currently issues only `capture:write` tokens. Catch does not currently issue the `full` tokens required by those operations.

tags.name: Pairing
tags.description: Pair supported clients to a scoped device token. Browser extensions use a nonce and verifier handshake; iOS Shortcuts use a setup code. There is no public device-listing API.

tags.name: Shortcut
tags.description: iOS Shortcut convenience endpoints. Every response contains exactly one flat string field: `result` on success or `error` on failure.

tags.name: CLI
tags.description: Browser-approved, read-only access for the Catch command-line client.

tags.name: Reserved full access
tags.description: Implemented capture-management routes that require a `full` token. No such token is currently issued through the public pairing flow.

get.description: Public operational probe. It does not expose account data.

post.description: Channel-neutral pairing endpoint intended for clients such as future Android apps or browser extensions. It does **not** list or manage devices. Device creation and listing remain signed-in frontend routes under `/devices`. A pairing code contains 10 numeric digits, expires after 15 minutes, and is consumed by a successful request. The response contains the only plaintext copy of the new device token.

201.description: Device paired. Store the returned token securely.

post.description: iOS-specific alias of `/api/devices/pair`. It uses the same pairing service but returns the flat Shortcut response envelope. On success, `result` is the new device token.

201.description: Device paired. `result` contains the device token.

401.description: Pairing code is invalid, expired, or has already been consumed.

post.description: Creates a short-lived browser pairing request. The client keeps the random verifier locally and sends only its SHA-256 base64url challenge here. Catch derives the user-facing browser/OS label from the request's ordinary User-Agent header. Open `pair_url` in a normal browser tab so the signed-in user can approve the device. No device token is placed in that URL.

post.summary: Poll or complete browser extension pairing
post.description: Proves possession of the verifier used to create the challenge. Returns HTTP 202 while user approval is pending. After approval, the response contains the only plaintext copy of the long-lived device token and consumes the pairing request.

200.description: Browser connected. Store the returned token in extension storage.

202.description: The request is still waiting for user approval.

post.description: Revokes the supplied device token by deleting its browser device. This endpoint accepts the extension's `capture:write` token.

get.description: Checks whether a device token still belongs to a connected browser device. Invalid and revoked tokens receive the same generic 401 response; the endpoint does not reveal token prefixes or partial matches.

post.description: Creates a short-lived verifier-protected authorization request and returns a browser URL. The URL contains no bearer credential.
Returns 202 until browser approval. After approval, returns the only plaintext copy of a long-lived read-only CLI token and consumes the request.

200.description: CLI authorized; the response contains the one-time plaintext token.

get.summary: Show the CLI account and device

200.description: Authenticated account and CLI device metadata.

post.summary: Submit a capture from iOS Shortcuts
post.description: iOS-friendly alias of `POST /api/v1/captures`. It uses the shared capture fields, but accepts at most one file in the singular multipart field `attachment`, matching the iOS Shortcuts `File` (`Datei`) value type. For a voice-to-text Shortcut without a recording, use `type=text` and place the transcript in `text`. To preserve the recording, use `type=audio`, send the audio file as `attachment`, and place the transcript in `extracted_text`. On success, `result` is the user's human-facing catch number, suitable for a message such as `Stored Catch #334`. Reusing `client_capture_id` for the same account returns the existing capture instead of creating a duplicate.

200.description: An idempotent retry found the existing capture. `result` contains its catch number.

201.description: Capture created. `result` contains its per-user catch number.

get.description: Requires `capture:read`. CLI authorization issues this read-only scope.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Capture state to list. Trash is selected by the presence of `deleted_at`, not by the stored status.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Case-insensitive text, URL, title, extracted text, or exact catch-number search.

200.description: Matching captures in descending creation order.

post.description: Client-neutral alias of `POST /api/shortcut/captures`. Both routes use the shared capture request documented below; only their response envelopes differ. A paired `capture:write` device token is sufficient. Reusing `client_capture_id` for the same account makes the request idempotent.

200.description: An idempotent retry found the existing capture.

get.description: Accepts either a per-user catch number or capture UUID and requires `capture:read`.

delete.description: Sets `deleted_at` and keeps the capture recoverable for 30 days. The stored status remains either `inbox` or `archived`. Requires a `full` token, which the public pairing flow does not currently issue.

post.description: Marks a capture as archived. Requires a `full` token, which the public pairing flow does not currently issue.

deviceToken.description: Device token returned once by a successful pairing request. The issued `capture:write` scope can submit captures.

cliToken.description: Long-lived, read-only token issued once by CLI browser authorization and stored by the client in the native OS credential service.

fullDeviceToken.description: Reserved `full` token. The application currently has no public flow that issues one.

CaptureId.name: id
CaptureId.description: Per-user catch number or server-generated capture UUID.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Supported by both capture aliases and used as `client_capture_id` when that body field is absent. For an iOS Shortcut form, supplying `client_capture_id` in the body is usually simpler. If neither value is supplied, Catch generates a random ID.

CaptureRequest.description: Versioned capture request. Choose `type` for known content, or use `unknown` when the client cannot classify it. This request supports multiple multipart attachments.

attachments[].description: Optional files. Repeat this field to send multiple files. For `type=unknown`, configured image and audio MIME types plus PDF are accepted; video, text-file, empty, and disguised attachments are rejected. Both each file and the combined unknown-capture attachments are limited to 15 MiB by the example configuration.

ShortcutCaptureRequest.description: iOS Shortcut request using the shared capture fields. Multipart requests accept one optional file in `attachment`. In Shortcuts, pass a `File` (`Datei`) value; OpenAPI represents that value as binary data. For `type=unknown`, Catch inspects the file and resolves the final stored type.

attachment.description: Optional single image or PDF supplied as an iOS Shortcuts `File` (`Datei`) value. The Shortcut endpoint rejects requests containing more than one uploaded file.

InvalidPairingCode.description: Pairing code is invalid, expired, or has already been consumed.

Unauthorized.description: Bearer token is absent, invalid, or lacks the required permission.

error.message: A token with the required permission is needed.

ShortcutUnauthorized.description: Bearer token is absent, invalid, or lacks `capture:write`.

example.error: A token with the required permission is needed.

ShortcutValidationFailed.description: Capture fields failed validation. Messages are flattened for iOS Shortcuts.

example.error: Provide text, a URL, or an attachment.

CaptureNotFound.description: No capture with that ID belongs to the authenticated account.

ApiFailure.description: The server could not complete the operation.

ShortcutFailure.description: The server could not complete the Shortcut operation.

example.error: The request could not be completed.

error.message: Database is not configured or unavailable.

example.error: Database is not configured or unavailable.

pairing_code.description: 10-digit code created for a setup-state device. It expires after 15 minutes. The optional displayed space or a hyphen is ignored.

code_challenge.description: Base64url-encoded SHA-256 digest of the random verifier retained by the extension.

code_verifier.description: Random verifier retained locally by the extension. It is never included in the approval URL.

pair_url.description: User-facing approval URL. It contains only the short-lived request ID.

ShortcutResponse.description: Mutually exclusive flat response for iOS Shortcuts.

client_capture_id.description: Optional stable ID generated by the client, unique for this logical capture. A non-blank body value takes precedence over `Idempotency-Key`. Save and reuse it when retrying the same capture to avoid duplicates. If both are absent, Catch generates a random `client_capture_...` value. Device tokens (`catch_device_...`) are never accepted as capture IDs.

title.description: Optional human-readable heading. It does not replace the required content in `text`, `url`, or an attachment.

text.description: Primary textual content. Put typed text and voice-to-text transcripts here. A non-blank value satisfies the content requirement.

url.description: Primary URL being captured. Use with `type=url`, or with `type=mixed` when the capture also has another primary content kind.

remote_attachment_url.description: Public image URL to retrieve as an attachment. Catch rejects private or reserved network targets and enforces the configured attachment size and MIME allowlist. Intended for browser image context-menu captures.

extracted_text.description: Optional machine-derived text that supplements the primary content, such as OCR from an image or a transcript from an attached recording. It may intentionally duplicate `text`. For known capture types this field alone does not satisfy the content requirement. For `type=audio`, the attachment remains the source and this field holds its transcript. For `type=unknown`, extracted-text-only input without an attachment is copied to `text`.
extracted_text.example: Recognized text from the attached image or audio.

source.description: Optional client/channel label for provenance. It is not an enum; use a stable value such as `ios-shortcut`. If omitted, the server stores `web`.

tags.description: Optional comma-separated tag names to assign after the capture is stored. Blank entries are ignored, duplicate names are assigned once, and new tags are created in lowercase.

metadata.description: Optional client-defined structured details. Send a JSON object with an application/json request, or a JSON-encoded object string with multipart/form-data. Metadata is stored but does not satisfy the content requirement.

CaptureInput.description: At least one of `text`, `url`, or a multipart attachment must normally contain data. For `type=unknown`, `extracted_text` may be the only textual value and is promoted to `text`. A title or metadata alone is not accepted. Voice-to-text example: `type=text`, `text=<dictated transcript>`, and `source=ios-shortcut`. Supplying a stable `client_capture_id` remains useful only for clients that can retry with the same value.

CaptureType.description: Required input classification: `text` for typed or dictated text (including a voice-to-text transcript with no retained recording); `url` for a link; `image` for image attachment(s); `audio` for an actual audio attachment whose transcript belongs in `extracted_text`; `file` for other attachment(s); `mixed` when multiple known primary kinds are intentionally combined; or `unknown` when the iOS Share Sheet input must be inspected by Catch. `unknown` is input-only and is replaced with a detected stored type. Unknown attachments accept configured image and audio MIME types plus PDF.

StoredCaptureType.description: Resolved type stored by Catch. `unknown` is never persisted.

CaptureStatus.description: Workflow state for active captures. Trash is represented separately by a non-null `deleted_at`.

CatchNumber.description: Immutable, monotonically increasing number scoped to the owning user. It is intended for human references such as `Catch #334`; the UUID remains the globally unique technical identifier.
